question: Should completed low-risk model-backed exec verdicts be reusable within one reviewer instance after the key is bound to the exact resolved executable and canonical node target?
rationale: The code can enforce a narrow reuse boundary, but whether an `allow-once` model verdict may authorize a later identical request is an exec security-policy decision rather than a purely mechanical optimization.

options.title: Fix identity and approve reuse
options.body: Forward the actual resolved executable from node preparation, add regression coverage for equal argv resolving to different binaries, and accept bounded low-risk reuse.

options.title: Retain per-call review
options.body: Reject reusable authorization verdicts and continue obtaining a fresh reviewer completion for every approval miss.

recommendation.title: Fix identity and approve reuse
recommendation.body: Forward the actual resolved executable from node preparation, add regression coverage for equal argv resolving to different binaries, and accept bounded low-risk reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history covers the node-host reviewer dispatch and documented executable-pinning boundary directly affected by this choice.
